topic: Vice-President — election and functions — mixed tiers
description: Article 63-71 — election, qualifications, ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, removal

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is elected by:

options.option_text: An electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (elected + nominated)

questions.explanation: Article 66 — Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of BOTH Houses of Parliament. Unlike the President's election, both ELECTED and NOMINATED members of Parliament participate. State legislators have NO role in VP's election. Method — single transferable vote, secret ballot, proportional representation. The 11th Amendment (1961) clarified the process.

questions.stem: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of:
questions.explanation: Article 64 — VP is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Presides over its sittings, casts a vote only in case of equality (casting vote). NOT a member of the House — does not vote ordinarily. When acting as President, he ceases to be Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Deputy Chairman presides). Lok Sabha is presided by the Speaker. The VP's salary (~₹4 lakh/month) is paid as Chairman of RS, not from CFI as President's is.

questions.stem: Which of the following qualifications is required for a person to become Vice-President but NOT President?

options.option_text: Qualified to be elected as a member of Rajya Sabha
Not holding any office of profit

questions.explanation: Article 66(3) — qualifications for VP: (i) citizen of India; (ii) at least 35 years of age; (iii) qualified for election as a MEMBER OF THE RAJYA SABHA (the unique requirement for VP). For President (Art 58), it's qualification to be a member of the LOK SABHA. Both must not hold any office of profit. Reason — VP presides over Rajya Sabha so RS-eligibility makes sense.

questions.stem: The Vice-President can be removed from office by a resolution passed by an effective majority in:

options.option_text: Rajya Sabha (effective majority) + Lok Sabha agreement (simple majority)

questions.explanation: Article 67(b) — VP can be removed by an 'effective majority' (more than half of the total members of the Rajya Sabha) AND agreed to by Lok Sabha by simple majority. 14 days' notice required. NO impeachment grounds prescribed (unlike for President — 'violation of Constitution'). The only constitutional officer who can be removed without specifying grounds. Resolution can ONLY originate in the Rajya Sabha (NOT in Lok Sabha).

questions.stem: When the Vice-President acts as President (during vacancy of President's office), he:

options.option_text: Continues as Chairman of Rajya Sabha simultaneously
Ceases to perform duties of Chairman, RS — the Deputy Chairman presides
Is automatically removed from VP post

questions.explanation: Article 65 — VP discharges President's functions during vacancy (death, resignation, removal, absence). During that time, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha (or any nominee) presides over RS sittings (Art 91). Maximum continuous period — 6 months — within which a new President must be elected. President's salary applies to acting VP for that period, not VP's salary. V.V. Giri (1969) and B.D. Jatti (1977) acted as President.

questions.stem: Which of these has NOT served as both President and Vice-President of India?
questions.explanation: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was President (2002-07) but never Vice-President. Those who held both posts: S. Radhakrishnan (VP 1952-62, P 1962-67); Zakir Husain (VP 1962-67, P 1967-69, died in office); V.V. Giri (VP 1967-69, P 1969-74); R. Venkataraman (VP 1984-87, P 1987-92); Shankar Dayal Sharma (VP 1987-92, P 1992-97); K.R. Narayanan (VP 1992-97, P 1997-2002); M. Hamid Ansari (VP 2007-17, never P); Venkaiah Naidu (VP 2017-22, never P).

questions.stem: The term of office of the Vice-President of India is:

options.option_text: 5 years from the date of entering office

questions.explanation: Article 67 — VP holds office for 5 years from the date of entering. Eligible for re-election any number of times (no limit; same as President). May resign at any time by writing to President. Continues in office despite expiry until successor enters. The President is also 5 years (Art 56). Casting vote and presiding privileges are stripped if acting as President under Art 65.
